title: v1.1 recruiter showcase: Home at a glance, cost what-if (illustrative), engine drill-down, plain-English help
audience: recruiters and hiring managers (business analytics, product, operations and supply chain) spending about 60 seconds on the app; engineers keep the technical depth on the About page and in the docs
rules: The Phase 8 spec (dashboards/phase8_spec.json) gains the engine and cost pages in the same commit as each page, copied from this file: the Phase 8 checks read every spec page, so listing a page before it exists would break them.
The app reads only dashboards/snapshots/ (frozen, sha256 in the manifest).
Every displayed number comes from a results file or a snapshot and is recomputed independently by dashboards/verify_v11.py (CI).
Phase 8 stays 5/5 and Phase 9 stays 10/10; their criteria are only extended, never loosened.
Generated docs only through python -m writeup.report_phase9; docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md stays the v1.0.0 body (Phase 9 W10); v1.1 notes go in docs/RELEASE_NOTES_v1.1.0.md.
No currency figure appears in README.md, docs/CASE_STUDY.md or any generated doc.

policy_chart.what: one chart comparing predictive / fixed interval / run to failure on simulated unplanned failures and simulated downtime hours (pooled, 200 machines)
policy_chart.source: oee_policies.csv rows scope=Pooled, kind=policy: unplanned_failures, downtime_hours
policy_chart.encoding: Okabe-Ito colour per policy plus the value printed on every bar and the policy named on the axis
policy_chart.label: title contains '(simulated)'

business_impact_row.title: Business impact (simulated)
business_impact_row.title_amendment: 2026-11-15, author-approved to fit V2.1 (check unchanged): the separate heading is not shown; the table's first column header 'Impact (simulated)' carries the label, and the three policy charts come before the table (shorter charts were tried: below 165 px the bars collapse, so the height is unchanged)

numbers.downtime_saved_vs_rtf: downtime hours, run to failure - predictive
numbers.wasted_life: wasted cycles, predictive vs fixed interval (both shown)

business_impact_row.review_amendment: 2026-11-15, author-approved after the Chrome review (checks unchanged): the table is a static table so its numbers stay visible at phone width; the wasted-life row reads 'Wasted engine life, cycles (simulated): predictive / other' with cells 'a / b'; the simulated notice reads 'Simulated plant: production, downtime and OEE are not measured data.' once instead of after a second 'Simulated.'
business_impact_row.independent: machines_phase6.csv re-aggregated, then the same differences

home.headline_labels: plain English, at most 60 characters, no dataset codes (FD00x) in a metric label; dataset codes only in captions; the forecast tile reads like 'Forecast error on engines the model never saw (lower is better)'

cost_page.title: What would each policy cost? (Illustrative)
cost_page.banner: Illustrative costs · Simulated plant · not real cost data

c_failure.label: Extra repair cost per unplanned failure

c_cycle.label: Cost per cycle of wasted engine life

cost_page.defaults_note: illustrative defaults, change them: round example values chosen for the demo, not taken from any data
cost_page.formula: total(policy) = downtime_hours x c_hour + planned_services x c_service + unplanned_failures x c_failure + wasted_cycles x c_cycle
cost_page.no_double_counting: downtime_hours already include the downtime of failures and services, so c_failure is only the extra repair cost of a failure, not its lost production time (stated on the page; unit-tested)
cost_page.module: app/cost.py (pure function, no Streamlit), unit-tested with hand-computed cases in tests/test_cost.py
cost_page.independent: verify_v11 recomputes totals and savings with its own arithmetic from machines_phase6.csv at the defaults and at 3 other input sets: all zeros, one cost at a time, and very large values
cost_page.tolerance: exact for integer inputs; relative 1e-12 otherwise
cost_page.currency: shown with '$' and the word 'illustrative'; never in README, case study or generated docs

engine_page.title: What happened to one engine, cycle by cycle?

filters.engine: every test engine of the chosen dataset (100 each)

engine_page.default_engine: FD001, the flagged engine with the lowest lower bound at its last cycle (ties: lowest engine id)

snapshot.rows: one per test cycle of FD001 and FD003 (29,692)
snapshot.built_by: dashboards/export_snapshots.py from data/raw/test_FD001.txt, test_FD003.txt and maintenance/forecasts_rolling_FD001.csv, FD003.csv
snapshot.precision: full (sensor values as in the NASA files; forecasts round-trip exact); about 2.7 MB
snapshot.independent: verify_v11 (and the CI verify job, which has the pinned data) compares it cell for cell with the raw files and the rolling forecasts

sensors.chosen_by: the four highest absolute correlations with remaining life in the EDA's training-data table (docs/EDA_FINDINGS.md)
sensors.names_source: A. Saxena, K. Goebel, D. Simon, N. Eklund, 'Damage Propagation Modeling for Aircraft Engine Run-to-Failure Simulation', PHM08, Table 2 (NASA NTRS 20090029214, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20090029214)
sensors.mapping_note: the data files number the sensors 1-21 without names; Table 2 lists the 21 outputs in order, and the order was checked against the data (s1 median 518.67 degR = T2 at sea level; s18 demanded fan speed = s8 physical fan speed 2388 rpm; s19 = 100 percent)

names.s11: Static pressure at HPC outlet (Ps30, psia)
names.s4: Total temperature at LPT outlet (T50, degR)
names.s12: Ratio of fuel flow to Ps30 (phi, pps/psi)
names.s7: Total pressure at HPC outlet (P30, psia)

numbers.label: forecast remaining life and its 90% interval at the last observed cycle
first cycle at which the interval's lower bound is at or below the alert threshold
flagged at the last observed cycle (yes/no)
numbers.independent: lower bound at last cycle <= threshold, recomputed

numbers.label: 'Service day N (one of 3 crew slots that day)' or 'not scheduled'
numbers.label_amendment: 2026-11-15, author-approved: day 0 reads 'Service today (day 0, one of 3 crew slots)'; 'Service day N' kept for N >= 1

charts: sensor trends (one small chart per sensor, axis titled with name and unit)
forecast mean with its 90% interval band and the alert line, axes titled with units
engine_page.simulated_label: the service-day line says the crew plan comes from the scheduler on real forecasts; no plant numbers on this page

plain_english_help.rule: each term has a one-line caption or tooltip wherever it first appears on a page; the About page keeps the full detail; every existing 'simulated' disclaimer stays
plain_english_help.where: the sentences live in app/common.py PLAIN and are shown as 'Term: sentence' (C.plain); verify_v11 scans each page's rendered text for them
plain_english_help.engine_note_amendment: 2026-11-15, author-approved: the drill-down states the RUL cap (facts.json rul_cap, from features/build.py RUL_CAP; re-derived by verify_phase8 from the clip value in models/predictions_phase5b.csv) and keeps one short sentence on replay vs final forecast above the chart; the MC dropout detail is in the interval tooltip and on About

readme.try_link: 'Try the live app' line directly after the one-line problem statement (Phase 9 W4 keeps the problem line first)
readme.hero: a screenshot of the v1.1 Home page (docs/figures/v11/), under 1 MB
readme.changes_note: a short 'v1.1 changes' section in the docs (generated)
